tasks.short: Identify operational requirements for new RFID systems.

steps.what: Observe item movements and interview operators to capture identification events, exceptions and operating conditions
Retrieve existing interface specifications, throughput records and applicable site constraints
Identify operational requirements for new systems to inform selection of technological solutions, resolving contradictory site needs
outputs: reasoned operational requirements and unresolved questions

steps.what: Prepare the requirements register with selected source links, acceptance fields and manually authored requirements
inputs: reasoned operational requirements and unresolved questions

steps.what: Approve the final requirements register and identify unresolved assumptions before baselining
Commit the approved operational requirements to the project baseline

tasks.design: Configure a requirements register in {OTHER}, the engineering requirements system, with source links to {DOCS} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Field reuse reduces lookup and register copying. Observations, interviews, requirement wording and acceptance judgement remain human. Final baselining is a separate action after the complete register exists. Changes invalidate approval. No model infers operating requirements from incomplete event logs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site findings and existing interface constraints are scattered across notes and operational screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked requirements fields and version baselines can reduce administrative work.
tasks.still_hard: Operational exceptions and contradictory stakeholder needs.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an actual operating requirement from a preferred technical solution.
tasks.altitude: Support requirements discovery without automating discovery judgement.

reach.learn: Use observed requirements and explicit unresolved assumptions.

evidence.claim: Requirements systems can link sources, reuse fields and baseline approved versions.

assumptions: s1 counts all new site capture. Existing operating records are produced in normal operations; missing data are investigated within retained work.
unknowns: Whether a native requirements register is already configured.
research_questions: Which copying steps remain in current requirements discovery?

already_counted.description: Site capture and final requirements review remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain register fields and source links.

approvals.approved_version: approved requirements version with open assumptions and baseline target

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Five lookup hours, three register preparation hours and five baseline-entry hours saved, less one upkeep hour; no additional gain if native functions already cover the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Integrate RFID tags, readers and software.

steps.what: Design the integration of tags, readers and software in radio frequency identification device designs
Prepare reader middleware configuration and tag-to-event mappings using native validated profiles
outputs: proposed bench configuration and target device list

steps.what: Approve the complete configuration, bench targets and rollback settings
inputs: proposed bench configuration and target device list

steps.what: Apply the approved configuration to the isolated internal RFID bench
Physically integrate the tags and readers, wiring and antenna arrangement on the bench
Test actual reads and software event delivery, diagnose exceptions and capture the resulting tested configuration
outputs: tested integration package and actual results

steps.what: Approve the final tested integration package for internal design record commitment
inputs: tested integration package and actual results

steps.what: Commit the approved tested integration package and results to the design repository

tasks.design: Reuse native profiles in {OTHER}, the RFID reader configuration and middleware suite with its engineering repository. The specialist adapts mappings and approves an exact bench configuration before application. Physical assembly and actual read/event tests remain manual. Test capture includes raw observations and corrections. A later approval covers the tested package, followed by a distinct design-record commit. Modified bench configurations return to s2 and s3. No production deployment or external transmission is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated reader configuration and copying tested settings into design records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exportable profiles and versioned configuration receipts provide deterministic reuse.
tasks.still_hard: RF behavior and integration failures depend on physical surroundings and device combinations.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose the assembled system rather than accept simulated compatibility.

ambition.what: Reuse integration setup while preserving actual bench verification.

tasks.altitude: Configuration assistance for hands-on RFID integration.

reach.learn: Use a tested configuration with actual event evidence.

evidence.claim: RFID reader utilities and middleware commonly offer reusable configuration profiles and event logs; cross-device portability must be checked.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and exclude unattended device runtime.
This is an internal isolated bench; production release requires a separate process.
s6 includes human observation and result capture. No new input capture is transferred to another role.
unknowns: Compatibility of installed readers with reusable profiles.
research_questions: Which integration parameters repeat without site-specific RF redesign?

already_counted.description: Bench authorization, actual tests and final record review.

incremental.description: Version and retest reusable profiles after firmware changes.

approvals.approved_version: approved bench configuration version including target devices and rollback settings
approved tested integration version including actual results and repository target

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Eight profile-preparation hours plus five application and ten record-entry hours saved, less two upkeep hours. Low case assumes existing profiles and record workflow already remove these activities.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Perform systems analysis of RFID technology using actual event traces, interfaces and failure reproduction
outputs: analyzed behavior and explicit software acceptance tests

steps.what: Draft RFID event-processing code and unit tests against the specialist's interface contract
inputs: analyzed behavior and explicit software acceptance tests
current source and reader SDK documentation

loop.purpose: Draft bounded event-parser and mapping changes
loop.input: Selected source, interface contract and acceptance tests
loop.check: Compile, run independent fixtures and inspect retry and duplicate-event behavior
loop.stop: Two repair attempts or any unexplained test discrepancy returns to manual coding
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native reader SDK examples and configuration first; only site-specific parsing or state logic needs a code draft.

steps.what: Run independent RFID trace replay and hardware checks and inspect mismatches
outputs: tested final patch and test evidence

steps.what: Review the final code and independent test evidence and approve the exact commit and internal test deployment
inputs: tested final patch and test evidence
internal test target and rollback plan
outputs: approved patch version and test target

steps.what: Commit the approved RFID code and test evidence to the internal source repository
inputs: approved patch version and test target

steps.what: Deploy only the approved committed code revision to the internal RFID test environment
inputs: approved patch version and test target

tasks.design: {OTHER} denotes the source editor, reader SDK, trace-replay test tools and internal source-control pipeline. Configure SDK examples and mapping options first. A bounded model loop drafts only unsupported site-specific code. The specialist captures and analyzes actual traces in s1, tests behavior with independent fixtures and hardware in s3, then approves the final code and test target. Separate actions commit and deploy to an isolated internal test environment. Code or target changes cancel approvals. Production release remains outside this proposal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site-specific event parsing and retry logic require repetitive code and test setup.
tasks.enabler_now: SDK scaffolds, reusable trace fixtures and bounded code drafting can reduce preparation work.
tasks.still_hard: Duplicate reads, missing events and timing behavior must match actual equipment behavior.
tasks.human_edge: Define the right system behavior and challenge superficially passing tests.

ambition.what: Implement current RFID behavior requirements with less routine coding effort.

tasks.altitude: A tested code drafting assistant with explicit internal release gates.

reach.learn: Keep independent device traces and acceptance fixtures.

evidence.claim: Code assistants can draft source and tests, while SDKs and trace replay supply deterministic scaffolding and checks; no task-specific productivity result is claimed.

assumptions: Shares and retained percentages are provisional, not measured.
Capture and diagnosis of real traces are fully counted in s1. Test fixture maintenance adds overhead below.
No unattended test runtime is treated as saved labour; s3 only reduces repeated human test setup.
Source is permitted in the chosen model environment; otherwise keep native scaffolding and drop the loop.
unknowns: Model draft quality for the installed SDK and protocol.
research_questions: Do independent regression results and review effort justify using the draft?

already_counted.description: Independent test execution and final code review remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain independent fixtures and check assistant failure cases.

approvals.approved_version: approved patch version including tests and source repository target
approved patch version and test target including rollback plan

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central savings are 12.25 coding, four test-setup and ten commit/deployment hours, less three upkeep. Low case assumes no preparation benefit and the same three-hour upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select RFID tags and placement locations.

steps.what: Survey item materials, handling, environmental exposure and candidate tag locations and capture observations
Filter the approved tag catalogue by verified material, frequency, durability and size constraints
outputs: candidate tag comparison with source links

steps.what: Test candidate tag placements on actual items across representative reader orientations and capture read behavior
inputs: candidate tag comparison with source links

steps.what: Select appropriate RFID tags and determine placement locations using the actual test results
inputs: candidate tag comparison with source links

steps.what: Write the exact selected tag specification and annotated placement record
Approve the final tag specification, placement annotations and design record target
Commit the approved tag and placement specification to the internal design record

tasks.design: Use verified catalogue filters in {OTHER}, the RFID tag comparison and reader-test software, with {SPREADSHEET} if native filters suffice. The specialist captures item constraints, checks supplier fields and tests placements physically. Missing catalogue values are checked manually in s2. Selection and exact annotated specification stay human. {DOCS} commits the final reviewed record through a separate native action. Changes void approval. No model predicts satisfactory read performance without physical tests.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual comparison of repeated tag datasheet fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue filters and controlled design-record filing reduce administrative work.
tasks.still_hard: Metal, liquid, orientation and real handling can invalidate nominal tag suitability.
tasks.human_edge: Judge representative placement tests and practical attachment constraints.

ambition.what: Reduce catalogue comparison without weakening physical selection tests.

tasks.altitude: Deterministic shortlist assistance for hands-on tag selection.

reach.learn: Use exact approved placement annotations and tag revisions.

evidence.claim: Tag catalogues and structured comparison sheets can filter known specification fields; actual RF suitability still requires local testing.

assumptions: All shares are provisional, not observed.
s1 and s3 include new observation and test-result capture; s2 includes checking missing and ambiguous supplier fields.
No tag purchase, production install or external recommendation send is proposed.
research_questions: How much comparison remains after existing catalogue filters?

already_counted.description: Physical tests, specification writing and final review remain counted.

incremental.description: Keep approved catalogue fields and revision references current.

approvals.approved_version: approved tag placement version including tag revision, annotations and target record

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Ten catalogue-comparison hours and two record-entry hours saved, less one upkeep hour; low case assumes these native functions are already in use.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: RFID engineering with native configuration reuse and controlled code assistance.
reach: Operations supplies real constraints; installation receives exact tested specifications.
role.ambitious_version: Reuse reliable configurations while retaining physical validation and system behavior ownership.
